newsitem.title: EGYPT: Wheat for Egypt probably on hold for inspection.
newsitem.headline: Wheat for Egypt probably on hold for inspection.

text.p: Rumours that Egypt has cancelled a wheat shipment probably arose from routine delays to wheat or flour cargoes for health inspections, a trader said on Thursday.
December wheat futures on the Chicago Board of Trade ended sharply lower on Wednesday because of the rumours.
The Cairo-based trader, Wayne Bacon of Oriac International, said he thought some U.S. soft red winter wheat was on hold on suspicion it contained high levels of scab (fusarium).
Some wheat flour, probably of French origin and bought by a private Alexandria company at $286 a tonne, was also on hold for similar reasons, he added.
"Flour is almost always put on hold for a month or so. It needs to be checked by the ministries of health and agriculture. If it was many cargoes, it might be significant," he added.
An official at the state's General Authority for Supply Authority, the main Egyptian grain buyer, said he had no information on any cancellation of a wheat shipment.
